scope: New primary-source-reviewed software compatibility, reimplementation, and archival-preservation projects. Each record identifies the exact application, software family, device protocol, or version targeted; unknown hardware/platform coverage is stated explicitly.

projects.title: WineVDM / OTVDM
projects.game: 16-bit Windows applications (Windows 1.x, 2.x, 3.0, and 3.1)
projects.platform: Win16 applications → 64-bit Windows
projects.status: Maintained compatibility emulator with stable v0.9.0 and rolling unstable builds. It combines CPU emulation with Wine-derived Win16-to-Win32 API conversion. Its DOS compatibility mode is explicitly incomplete; the project recommends DOSBox or MS-DOS Player for DOS programs.
projects.summary: Runs historical 16-bit Windows applications on 64-bit Windows by emulating the CPU and translating Win16 APIs to Win32. The repository is an altered WineVDM build with install integration and compatibility fixes; it is a compatibility runtime, not a recovered original application.
projects.strategy: CPU emulation plus Wine-derived Win16-to-Win32 API conversion and compatibility fixes
projects.source_available: Public source under GPL-2.0; stable v0.9.0 release and unstable CI builds. Historical Win16 application binaries are separate.
projects.subtype: Win16 application compatibility emulator

projects.title: Open-Turzx
projects.game: Closed-source TURZX 2.8-inch USB dashboard software, firmware turzx_0001_0024
projects.platform: TURZX 480×480 USB display; Windows and Linux supported, macOS untested
projects.status: The maintained Python app documents a working device daemon, layout editor, sensor displays, and reverse-engineered USB protocol on Windows and Linux. macOS is untested; PyPI/AUR packaging is still listed as planned rather than released.
projects.summary: Replaces the closed, Windows-only TURZX screen application with a cross-platform driver and dashboard for the 2.8-inch 480×480 USB display. The README identifies USB VID:PID 1CBE:0028 and firmware turzx_0001_0024; the project documents a DES-CBC protocol and its reverse-engineering history.
projects.strategy: Reverse-engineered USB protocol and independent Python dashboard/driver implementation
projects.source_available: Public source under MIT. The proprietary vendor application is not included.
projects.subtype: Closed hardware companion app reimplementation / USB device driver

projects.title: TRCC Linux
projects.game: Thermalright LCD Control Center (TRCC) 2.1.2 device-control software
projects.platform: Thermalright TRCC functionality on Linux; v9.10.4 release page also lists Windows and macOS packages
projects.status: Active source project with v9.10.4 packages published on 2026-09-26 for Linux distributions, Windows, and macOS. The README still solicits testers across operating systems, so coverage should be checked per device rather than inferred from the package list.
projects.summary: A source reimplementation of the Thermalright LCD Control Center interface for controlling LCD and LED devices. The technical reference enumerates supported USB/SCSI/HID device identifiers and transport families; the upstream project asks users to submit test reports for unverified hardware.

projects.title: Pichau Aqua 240X Linux Driver
projects.game: Pichau PC SmartMonitor LED display protocol for the Aqua 240X AIO cooler
projects.platform: Linux over USB serial device 1A86:484A
projects.status: Early project with four commits and no packaged release. The maintainer reports real-hardware testing on Ubuntu 24.04 with Intel coretemp and NVIDIA nvidia-smi; AMD sensors and other distributions are implemented but explicitly unverified.
projects.summary: Independently reimplements the proprietary Windows PC SmartMonitor LED protocol as a small Linux Python driver for the Pichau Aqua 240X pump display. Its protocol note documents recovery from the vendor Windows application and empirical verification of a temperature frame on the physical display. Other coolers are only candidates if they use the same USB chip.
projects.strategy: Protocol reverse engineering of the Windows application followed by an independent USB-serial driver
projects.source_available: Public source under MIT; no vendor Windows code or binaries are included or required.
projects.subtype: AIO cooler display companion application / Linux driver

projects.title: Fifine AmpliGame D6 Driver
projects.game: Fifine AmpliGame D6 15-key LCD stream deck vendor software/protocol
projects.platform: Linux tested; Windows implementation untested; macOS unsupported
projects.status: Small early project; Linux is tested, Windows code is explicitly untested, and macOS integration is absent. The maintainer reports the device degrades with repeated image writes: after a power cycle, successive draws rendered 15, then 4, then 0 keys in the documented test, so the repository advises one redraw per physical power cycle.
projects.summary: Reverse-engineered driver and key editor for the Fifine AmpliGame D6 stream deck, replacing its missing Linux vendor support. It uses the documented HID MOD 1/MOD 2 protocol to control 15 LCD keys and contains a clear hardware wear/refresh limitation that should be visible to users.
projects.strategy: Reverse-engineered HID protocol and independent driver/editor
projects.source_available: Public MIT source; the vendor application is not required.
projects.subtype: Stream deck companion software reimplementation / HID driver

projects.title: wCopy NFC Linux
projects.game: wCopy Smart Reader / NSR106-IDIC V NFC dongle (VID:PID 0416:B030)
projects.platform: Linux USB-HID via hidraw
projects.status: Public Linux toolkit documents read, key-check, dump/restore, UID writing, formatting, a GTK GUI, and libnfc/mfoc bridging. The author says the protocol was recovered from a Windows USBPcap capture and disassembly of nfcPro_wbw.exe; writes and formatting can alter cards, so the README requires ownership or explicit authorization and recommends a backup.
projects.summary: Reimplements the proprietary Windows reader software's USB-HID/PN532 protocol as a Linux driverless CLI and optional GUI. The README supports the 0416:B030 reader and gives explicit safety boundaries for MIFARE Classic cards.
projects.strategy: USB capture and binary analysis followed by independent Python protocol implementation
projects.source_available: Public MIT source; the proprietary Windows application is not distributed.
projects.subtype: NFC reader desktop utility reimplementation / USB-HID driver

projects.title: wCopy NFC for Mac
projects.game: wCopy / NSR106-IDIC V USB NFC reader protocols (VID:PID 0416:B008 and 0416:B030)
projects.platform: Native macOS 13+ using IOKit HID
projects.status: Native SwiftUI and CLI tools implement the Linux project's reverse-engineered USB-HID/PN532 protocol. The B008 handshake is verified on a physical V601 reader; B030 is supported using the same protocol, whose hardware verification is attributed to the Linux upstream. Some card attack/write paths have explicit hardware-testing limits in the README.
projects.summary: Ports the wCopy NFC reader workflow to native macOS, replacing the vendor's Windows-only client without a kernel driver, GTK, hidraw, or Python runtime. The repository distinguishes device enumeration from a confirmed protocol-ready state and documents conservative card-write defaults.
projects.strategy: Native Swift implementation of the protocol reverse-engineered by the Linux project
projects.source_available: Public MIT source; protocol implementation credits and derives from the separate MIT-licensed Linux project.
projects.subtype: Native macOS NFC reader companion application / USB-HID driver

projects.title: Panelbeater
projects.game: Fujitsu/Ricoh ScanSnap iX1500 touchscreen panel host and scan workflow
projects.platform: Linux over Wi-Fi or USB
projects.status: Python utility tested on a real iX1500 over Wi-Fi (USB scan path also documented). iX1400/iX1600 compatibility is described as probable, not tested. Wi-Fi network scanning is fixed at 300 dpi color while USB resolution is adjustable; a USB cable disables the network registration path.
projects.summary: Reimplements the ScanSnap iX1500 touchscreen panel protocol so the physical Scan button can launch a scan on Linux without the vendor application. It enrolls a Linux host, receives panel jobs, builds PDFs, and optionally runs OCR; the protocol document explains the device's network and USB behaviors.
projects.strategy: Reverse-engineered touchscreen-panel and scan-host protocol implementation
projects.source_available: Public GPL-2.0 source; no vendor software required.
projects.subtype: Document scanner panel/scan-client reimplementation

projects.title: ScanSnap
projects.game: Fujitsu ScanSnap and fi-series scanners, including S1500M, iX1600, iX1500, iX1400, and iX1300
projects.platform: Native macOS 26+ with direct USB scanner support
projects.status: Native Swift app with an MIT license and a hardware compatibility matrix. The README marks S1500M and iX1600 as working/validated; iX1500, iX1400, and iX1300 reuse the same documented protocol profile but are explicitly not tested on their own hardware. Older S300-family acquisition paths remain preliminary.
projects.summary: Reimplements a modern native macOS scan application and direct USB protocol support for older Fujitsu ScanSnap and fi-series devices, with no vendor scanning utility in the scan path. The project identifies exact scanner models and separates physically tested profiles from inferred protocol-family compatibility.
projects.strategy: Native Swift scanner client with reverse-engineered direct USB protocol profiles
projects.source_available: Public MIT source. Some scanner models require user-supplied firmware; the project says those firmware images are copyrighted and not bundled.
projects.subtype: Legacy scanner desktop application reimplementation / native macOS driver

projects.title: AirScap
projects.game: Fujitsu/Ricoh ScanSnap iX500 VENS Wi-Fi scanning client
projects.platform: Wi-Fi ScanSnap iX500 → eSCL/AirScan clients on macOS, Linux, and Windows
projects.status: Go protocol bridge; iX500 is the only scanner reported physically tested, using macOS Image Capture. The README says other VENS-compatible ScanSnap models and SANE/Windows clients are not yet verified. It exposes the scanner as a local eSCL device and has Debian/Ubuntu release packages.
projects.summary: Reimplements the ScanSnap iX500's proprietary VENS network protocol from captured official-app traffic and translates it into standard eSCL/AirScan for modern clients. This restores Wi-Fi scanning after the iX500's former ScanSnap Connect Application was discontinued and the current ScanSnap Home dropped that model.
projects.strategy: Captured-traffic VENS protocol reimplementation with an eSCL/AirScan compatibility bridge
projects.source_available: Public MIT source; no proprietary scanner application or binary is included.
projects.subtype: Discontinued scanner app replacement / Wi-Fi protocol bridge

projects.title: Ricoh / PFU SP-1130N Network Driver for macOS
projects.game: Ricoh/PFU SP-1130N network scanner using PaperStream FCL
projects.platform: Network scanner bridge to local eSCL/AirScan on macOS; macOS 26 on Apple Silicon physically tested
projects.status: A newly released Python-built bridge reports a successful physical scan from the SP-1130N on Apple Silicon/macOS 26. Intel binaries are CI-built but not hardware-tested, and related SP-series models are explicitly unverified. The installer is unsigned/not notarized and installs a system LaunchDaemon.

The maintainer says the implementation was derived from observed behavior and official-driver analysis and does not redistribute vendor binaries or firmware.

projects.title: Canon PIXMA G3010 CHMP Linux Scanner
projects.game: Canon PIXMA G3010 proprietary CHMP 1.4.0 scan protocol
projects.platform: Linux network scanning over the printer's HTTP/HTTPS interface
projects.status: An early Python client implements an end-to-end G3010 scan sequence after 27 protocol probes. The README gives an exact model-specific scope and notes that broader G-series support is future work; HTTPS requires limiting the connection to TLS 1.2 for this printer's embedded server.
projects.summary: Reimplements Canon's undocumented CHMP 1.4.0 scanner protocol for the PIXMA G3010, enabling Linux network scanning without the Windows/macOS utility, vendor driver, or SANE backend. This repository is distinct from pixma-rs: it is a small Linux Python client, while pixma-rs is a separate native macOS print/scan bridge.
projects.strategy: Black-box HTTP/TLS protocol probing and independent CHMP 1.4.0 client implementation
projects.source_available: Public source repository; no Canon application is needed. No explicit source license was identified in the repository metadata reviewed.
projects.subtype: Printer/scanner vendor-protocol reimplementation

projects.status: Public driver source replaces the vendor's unavailable 64-bit driver path and fixes a 32-bit driver issue that prevented operation on Windows Vista and later. The repository contains firmware loader, scanner driver, model resources, and installer components; no packaged release is listed on the README page.

projects.status: Explicit proof of concept: the maintainer says firmware load, scan transport, and negative-to-positive image pipeline work end to end, while the UI is far from finished. Users must provide Kodak firmware for their hardware revision; it is not bundled.

projects.title: Pakon
projects.game: Kodak/Pakon F-135 and F-135+ 35mm film scanners
projects.platform: macOS 13+ Apple Silicon app; source build also supports Linux, with Windows build planned
projects.status: The README marks the F-135 as fully working. F-135+ scans using settings recorded from another F-135+ and currently have fewer options. F-235/F-335 are explicitly unsupported. Kodak's color engine/assets are used as-is under separate third-party terms, and Digital ICE remains listed as upcoming.
projects.summary: Replaces the aging Kodak/Pakon scanner client with a modern Mac application and source-buildable scanner workflow. It reconstructs the USB/protocol host side, performs film framing and exports JPEG/TIFF/raw scans; the repository separates AGPL project code from Kodak firmware, binaries, profiles, and other third-party material.
projects.strategy: Reverse-engineered userspace USB protocol and source-reimplemented scanner client

projects.platform: macOS, Windows, and Linux userspace driver/application
projects.status: Highly experimental and explicitly WIP. The project reports an unresolved brightness offset, a production Go renderer still using a placeholder while the Python engine has the verified tone chain, broken black-and-white scanning, and no real-hardware verification for F-235/F-335. The app UI is unfinished.

The maintainer documents live emulation and physical-hardware checks against the original Kodak DLLs, but the remaining rendering and model-coverage gaps mean this is an active research implementation rather than a dependable finished scanner app.

projects.title: pakon-tlx-macos
projects.game: Kodak TLXClientDemo / F-X35 COM stack for Pakon F-135 scanners
projects.platform: Original 32-bit Windows XP-era client via Wine 11 on macOS 15+; Apple Silicon or Intel
projects.status: The maintainer reports it works on a base F-135 and has been confirmed by other owners on an F-135+ and another base unit. F-235/F-335 are untried. It replaces the kernel USB-driver calls with a libusb shim, while the Kodak client and imaging DLLs remain unmodified and must be supplied externally.
projects.summary: Runs the genuine Windows Kodak TLX scanner client on modern macOS by using Wine and translating its five Pakon135 kernel-driver calls through a local shim to libusb. It preserves the vendor's imaging and Digital ICE behavior rather than reimplementing the full scanner app; OEM software and firmware are required from a source trusted by the user.
projects.strategy: Wine compatibility plus a Win32 kernel-driver API shim to libusb
projects.source_available: Public MIT bridge source. It contains no Kodak code or firmware, but it requires the external proprietary TLX client, DLLs, and firmware.

projects.title: Huion Note X10 Linux BLE Driver and Note Extractor
projects.game: Huion Note X10 (internal HUION_T218) BLE driver and offline-note protocol
projects.platform: Linux with BlueZ 5.x plus a documented BlueZ patch
projects.status: The maintainer reports end-to-end hardware validation on NixOS for pen pressure/tilt and extraction of stored notes. It requires a small patch for a Huion firmware BLE quirk. By default, successfully exported pages are deleted from the tablet unless the user passes --keep.
projects.summary: Reverse-engineers the Huion Note X10 BLE protocol from vendor drivers and Android captures, then supplies a Linux tablet driver and local note exporter. The driver sends pen events through uinput; the exporter converts stored strokes into SVG/PNG/JSON without the Huion app or cloud.
projects.strategy: Vendor driver/APK analysis and BLE capture-based protocol reimplementation
projects.source_available: Public MIT source, including protocol notes and an optional BlueZ patch. Decompilation artifacts and personal captures are gitignored.

projects.title: TP-Link JetStream USB Console for Linux
projects.game: TP-Link TL-SG3428 v2.20 USB console / BootUtil v1.0.0 firmware dated 2025-02-13
projects.platform: Linux raw USB using libusb
projects.status: A one-file Python tool reports testing on a TP-Link TL-SG3428 v2.20 with BootUtil v1.0.0 firmware. It supports terminal access and an automated password/factory reset path. Factory reset erases switch configuration; README also lists related USB-ID models as expected rather than tested compatibility.
projects.summary: Reimplements the undocumented USB console path for a JetStream managed switch because TP-Link's Windows-only driver is unavailable on Linux. The reverse-engineering notes show that the device advertises vendor-specific USB class but responds to CDC ACM baud-rate requests; the utility uses raw USB bulk endpoints instead of a kernel serial driver.
projects.strategy: USB request probing and direct CDC ACM-over-libusb console implementation
projects.source_available: Public MIT source; no TP-Link driver is distributed.
projects.subtype: Managed network switch driver and service utility reimplementation

projects.summary: Reverse-engineers the proprietary Keydous control software and implements direct Linux keyboard configuration without a Windows daemon. It includes an extensive device-protocol reference and a web GUI for key maps, lighting, display images, profiles, and power settings.
projects.strategy: Vendor application analysis followed by raw HID/BLE protocol reimplementation
projects.source_available: Public MIT source and protocol documentation.
